r1.context:
Your school is organising a film festival. Decide which film would be best for each person based on their preferences and the film descriptions (A–F). Use each film description only once. There is one film you do not need to use.
FILMS
A) A man’s job is to enter people’s dreams to find out their secrets. But when he is asked to put a specific thought into someone’s head during their sleep, things get complicated. The line between the real world and dreams begins to blur, and nothing is easy to understand anymore.
B) A life told in key moments – a childhood kitchen, the first heartbreak, a silent car ride. This is a story of finding oneself in the quiet and beautiful moments. It’s a reflection on the memories and mistakes that shaped a person into who they are today.
C) A puppy runs away after something tragic happens to his family. After growing up alone, he finally decides to go back and face what he left behind. With support from his friends, he learns how to become the leader of the pack.
D) A man loses his memory and wants to solve the mystery of what happened to him. He uses notes and pictures to help remember things and face reality. The story has a strange storyline that runs in reverse, but, in the end, the whole story is revealed.
E) Two people from very different backgrounds meet by chance on a plane. Even though they do not have a lot in common, they fall in love. But soon, real life challenges strain their relationship. Will they stay together?
F) After a huge loss, a group of heroes has one final chance to change everything. Despite their differences, they must work together and make difficult choices. The final battle pushes them to their limits as they try to save the world. 2026

r2.context:
Read the article about how to write a blog and choose the answer (A, B, C or D) which fits best.
BLOG WRITING TIPS Know your why. Why do you want to blog? Perhaps you want to inspire or educate others, raise awareness about a cause that is important to you, promote your business or connect with a like-minded community? Of course, you may have multiple reasons. I certainly do. However, I believe it’s invaluable to be clear of your purpose from the start, even if this evolves over time.
Look outwards & inwards. When I first started blogging, I essentially used it as a diary, a place to document my thoughts about my interests. There is absolutely nothing wrong with this if a personal record is your only goal. However, if you want to grow an audience, then you need to find a way to connect with your readers. Why should they care about your story? My blogs often start with a personal experience, but then I balance this with some wider context, such as adding some researched statistics. If I’m sharing something that has added value in my life, then I will share tips and advice on how my readers could include this in their life.
Invest in your writing. One of the best tips I got when I started blogging was to act like your blog has thousands of readers from day one. If you take it seriously, then others will too. This means it’s always worthwhile investing time to improve your writing. Don’t view it as a boring task, but as a key part of your work. Every time you edit, you are showing respect – for your topic, for your readers, and for your own ability to communicate something meaningful.
Open strong. Titles are key, so use them wisely. I usually redraft my titles numerous times until I find one that both clearly states what the blog will be about whilst also attracting readers to open it. This takes practise, so don’t worry too much about getting it perfect. Additionally, make sure you put some real thought into your opening sentence. Like titles, a well-crafted opening sentence or paragraph will keep people reading.
Read for inspiration. There is some famous advice “If you want to be a writer, you must do two things above all others: read a lot and write a lot.” I personally think reading is key. Reading is not only a pleasure, but it’s also crucial if you want to become a good writer. Any reading is beneficial, but I find it extremely useful to find other blogs that write about similar subjects. It shows you what works and what doesn’t. You can see how other writers connect with readers and get ideas for your own posts. This kind of focused reading teaches while also inspiring you.
Finish strong. Think of your ending as the final thought you leave with your reader. Avoid introducing any new ideas here. Restate your main point in one clear sentence. Then, ask a direct question to encourage thinking and comments – this turns readers into active participants. When people comment, they invest in your blog’s community. Remember, a strong ending isn’t just a conclusion; it’s the start of a discussion. Reflect often. If you are writing regularly, it’s easy to keep working towards the next deadline without taking any time to reflect. However, reflection is crucial as it allows time to notice growth, highlight areas you would like to improve, and inform what you want to write about next. This is especially important if you want to grow your readership and maybe even commercialize your blog. I schedule reflection at the beginning of each month. This is where I review my analytics (such as views, engagement, and audience demographics) and note down what I’ve learnt from this before moving on to planning my next post. 2026

r3.context:
Fill in the gaps (14–20) in the text with the missing sentences (A–H). There is one sentence you do not need to use.
AN APPLE A DAY KEEPS THE DOCTOR AWAY You have probably heard the saying: “An apple a day keeps the doctor away.” (14) ______. But where does this expression come from, and is there any truth behind it?
People have always had a strong belief in the healing power of food. (15) ______. Apples are nutritional fruits, which were grown in many yards and could be stored all winter, so they were readily available and were seen as an easy and effective way to support health.
The roots of the expression date back to 19th-century Wales. At that time, it appeared as: “Eat an apple on going to bed, and you’ll keep the doctor from earning his bread.” However, over time the phrase changed to “an apple a day keeps the doctor away”. (16) ______. This version was shorter and easier to remember, which helped it spread beyond Wales and into common usage in English-speaking countries around the world. Passed from parent to child, teacher to student, and friend to friend, it became part of the language and has remained one of the most recognized health sayings for over a century. Even now, in a world full of health apps, supplements, and modern medicine, the old proverb has not lost its charm. (17) ______. Of course, no one believes that apples alone can prevent illness, but they do have many benefits. These fruits are rich in fibre, which helps your stomach work properly. Though apples are not the most vitamin-dense fruits overall, they contain a variety of vitamins and nutrients. (18) ______. Apples have long been associated not only with health, but also with knowledge and even mystery. From the biblical story of Adam and Eve to the legend of Isaac Newton and his discovery of gravity, apples have represented learning and discovery. In Greek mythology, apples were sacred fruits connected with love and beauty. In Norse myths, they were believed to give eternal youth. (19) ______. Its familiar image is now instantly recognizable in corporate logos and the narratives of our favourite films and books. This shows how a simple fruit can carry deep, shared meanings, bridging ancient myths and contemporary culture.
Although the old saying about an apple a day keeping the doctor away may not be entirely true, it is still useful advice. (20) ______ . Apples are a nutritional powerhouse, packed with essential fibre, vitamins, and antioxidants. Therefore, while it may not literally eliminate doctors’ visits, making an apple a daily part of your diet is a simple and effective step toward overall wellness, supporting the saying’s core wisdom. 2026

tasks.text:
You saw this announcement on a teenage lifestyle website and have decided to write an article about the topic.
How do you stay connected with your friends?
Today’s teenagers use many ways to keep in touch with their friends. We are looking for articles from teenagers. We want to know how you build and maintain friendships in today’s world.
Send us your article in which you answer these questions:
• How do teenagers build and maintain friendships in today’s world?
• How do you usually keep in touch with your friends? Why do you do it this way?
• How do you show your friends that you value the connection you have?
Write an article answering the questions in the announcement.
Write around 200 words. You have 40 minutes to complete the task.
